name: Ruins of Stardust
summary: On an island south of Astranaar, the Ruins of Stardust lie under Felwood's spreading corruption. Bog beasts prowl the fallen sanctuary, but stardust shrubs still grow among its stones with healing power.

sections.title: A Blighted Sanctuary
sections.body: South of Astranaar, you find the Ruins of Stardust on a solitary island. The night elves once held this holy place in reverence. Now a sickly yellow-green hue clouds the water, stained by demonic rot draining south from Felwood, as at nearby Iris Lake. Local plant life has twisted into hostile bog beasts. They prowl the fallen masonry, their temperaments warped by the tainted lake.

sections.title: The Enduring Stardust
sections.body: Stardust shrubs still bloom among the ruins, untouched by the corruption in the soil and along the shore. Their leaves and blossoms can cleanse and heal. Shamans, herbalists, and local night elf defenders seek them for remedies against Ashenvale's encroaching decay.

faq.q: What were the Ruins of Stardust originally used for?
faq.answer: The night elves once tended the Ruins of Stardust as sacred holy ground. Its marble pillars and lakeside perch offered a tranquil place of reverence before demonic corruption took root in the forest.

faq.q: Why is the water around the island discolored?
faq.answer: Demonic corruption flows from Felwood's blighted peaks into Ashenvale's waterways and taints the lake. The water turns murky yellow-green, disturbing its natural balance.

faq.q: What makes the stardust shrubs special?
faq.answer: Stardust shrubs remain pure in soil soaked by demonic runoff. They resist the surrounding taint and can restore and heal, making them valuable in cleansing rituals.
Large, corrupted bog beasts wander the island. The tainted water has warped these nature elementals from peaceful forest guardians into aggressive threats that lumber through the shallows.

angles.text: As a shaman, you can use uncorrupted stardust as a cleansing reagent in spiritual trials, including the Call of Water trials to master the restorative elements.
As a night elf, you see a former sanctuary falling to Felwood's slow, putrid runoff. Its fate reminds you of the struggle to protect Ashenvale from enduring demonic corruption.
